boundary_refinements.muslim:2170: Retain the explicit parenthetic Umm Atiyya subject at the opening of Ibn Ulayya variant: it materially distinguishes the report speaker from the transmitting Ibn Ulayya.
boundary_refinements.muslim:2174: Retain the explicit parenthetic Umm Atiyya subject in the resumed braid fragment; the intervening compiler bridge does not make her actual supplied attribution expendable.

bukhari:2157.hi: Jarir describes his pledge to the Messenger: testimony, prayer, zakat, listening/obedience and goodwill to every Muslim. The designated-leader parenthesis supplies the antecedent of his and limits the obedience clause; retain it as necessary source scope, with all honorifics.
bukhari:2157.ur: Jarir describes the same complete pledge in this own Urdu field. The printed designated-amir parenthesis limits listening and supplies the referent of his obedience; retain it, not an unrestricted command to obey everyone.

bukhari:2159.hi: Ibn Umar transmits the explicit Messenger prohibition of a townsman selling a rural person goods. The final Ibn Abbas said the same sentence is only a parallel pointer and supplies no second independent body.
bukhari:2159.ur: The complete Ibn Umar prohibition is supplied. The closing یہی ابن عباس statement is a same-content reference, not another quoted report to expand or count.

bukhari:2161.hi: Anas says we were forbidden to let a townsman sell a rural person trade goods. The authority who forbade them is not named in this field; preserve the passive report without inserting the Prophet.
bukhari:2161.ur: Anas explicitly states the finite passive prohibition. No named prohibiting speaker occurs in this own text; retain the actual Anas testimony and unknown authority.

bukhari:2162.hi: Abu Hurayra transmits two explicit Prophetic prohibitions. The trading-caravan parenthesis is the only supplied object of going out to meet and materially limits the first prohibition; retain it.
bukhari:2162.ur: Both prohibitions are explicitly attributed to the Prophet. The caravan object in parentheses defines the group being intercepted, so it remains with that instruction.

bukhari:2163.hi: Tawus asks Ibn Abbas about the expressly cited Prophetic rural-sale prohibition; Ibn Abbas actually replies not to be his broker. Keep question/citation and the Companion explanatory reply as distinct components of this one dialogue.
bukhari:2163.ur: The transmitter question and Ibn Abbas broker answer are actually narrated dialogue. Distinguish the explicitly cited Prophetic prohibition from Ibn Abbas own interpretation; no later compiler gloss is present.

bukhari:2164.hi: Ibn Masud supplies the goat-return ruling, including the finite return instruction in parentheses and one sa without a commodity supplied. The separately stated Prophetic caravan prohibition is a second report component.
bukhari:2164.ur: The printed return-the-goat parenthesis is an operative part of Ibn Masud instruction and stays. The following Prophet prohibition of meeting caravan people is separately attributed; do not label the first ruling as direct Prophetic speech.

bukhari:2167.ar: The complete Arabic gives Abdullah report that people bought food at the upper market and resold it in place; the Messenger forbade that until they moved it. Admit this own full finite report. It does not explicitly say their places, and that English qualification is not inserted.
bukhari:2167.en: The complete English describes buying food at the head of the market and the Apostle prohibition until they brought it to their places. The their parenthesis restricts the destination and remains literal. Admit its own wording without harmonizing the Arabic.
bukhari:2167.hi: The entire Hindi field duplicates the Musaddad/Yahya/Ubaydullah/Nafi/Ibn Umar chain and stops at that. It contains no market or food report body. Keep the full damaged chain as reviewed context; do not translate the Arabic or English into it.
bukhari:2167.ur: The complete Urdu field likewise repeats the chain twice and ends with کہ. No substantive report predicate follows. Retain it as context, with no missing body filled.
bukhari:2167.ur-Latn: The entire Roman Urdu duplicates the same chain and ends ke with no body. This was actually read, not inferred from Hindi or Urdu; preserve it as reviewed context.

bukhari:2180.hi: Abu al-Minhaj, as actually printed in Hindi, asks Bara and Zayd about bay al-sarf. Their mutual better-knowledge remarks precede their explicit Prophetic gold-for-silver-on-credit prohibition. The parenthetic definition of sarf is glossary context. Preserve the printed narrator name without Urdu repair.
bukhari:2180.ur: Abu al-Minhal asks Bara and Zayd; each defers to the other before both report the Prophet prohibition. The sarf gold/silver-exchange gloss is separate context; the actual quotation states its own gold/silver and credit scope.

bukhari:2181.hi: This separate ID independently supplies the complete same-looking Hindi dialogue and prohibition, including the source Abu al-Minhaj name. Keep it separate from2180; glossary definition alone is context.
bukhari:2181.ur: This separate occurrence supplies its own Abu al-Minhal question, mutual deference and explicit Prophetic prohibition. It is not merged with2180 even though the full wording matches. Sarf definition is context.

bukhari:2182.hi: Abu Bakra reports the Prophet silver/silver and gold/gold equal-quantity rule and the two reciprocal gold/silver permissions. Preserve the source conditions exactly; no absent hand-to-hand clause is added.
bukhari:2182.ur: The complete Abu Bakra report contains equal-for-equal restrictions and reciprocal cross-metal permissions. All clauses are supplied report content, with no appended explanation.

bukhari:2187.hi: Ibn Abbas transmits the explicit Prophetic prohibition of muhaqala and muzabana. The field supplies no definitions or external references; keep it whole without adding them.
bukhari:2187.ur: The short Urdu field is a complete chain and explicit prohibition. Neither term receives an appended definition; retain its exact words.

bukhari:2189.hi: Jabir transmits the date-ripeness prohibition and barter limitation with the ariya exception. Preserve damaged chain wording and omitted names. The dry-fruit parenthesis restricts the otherwise broad any-other-thing phrase and is retained as material transaction scope.
bukhari:2189.ur: The own Urdu chain names Ibn Jurayj and Ata; do not copy those into Hindi. Keep all conditions and the ariya exception. Dry fruit limits the forbidden exchange category rather than merely renaming a technical term.

bukhari:2196.hi: Jabir report includes the actual question about tashah and the Prophet yellow/red edible-ripeness answer. Retain the dialogue; the final fruit-maturity-is-meant parenthesis repeats an explanatory definition and remains context.
bukhari:2196.ur: The Arabic-script technical word within Urdu and the supplied question/answer remain literal. The final parenthetic ripeness gloss is redundant commentary, distinct from the actual answer.

bukhari:2203.hi: Abu Abdullah transmits through Ibrahim/Hisham/Ibn Abi Mulayka a Nafi ruling about pollinated dates, slave and field. This is an attributed Nafi saying, with no Prophetic attribution. The Imam Bukhari identity parenthesis is context. The final confirmation that Nafi named all three remains transmission scope.
bukhari:2203.ur: The own Urdu field attributes the finite sale ruling to Nafi. Preserve its spelling بیجا and all three categories. Abu Abdullah identifying parentheses are commentary; the final three-category confirmation stays with the narrated ruling.

bukhari:2205.hi: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet muzabana prohibition, then specifies three actual transaction cases and closes by expressly saying the Prophet forbade all those kinds. The yani passage defines the scope of this supplied prohibition, not a detached dictionary footnote; retain the whole report and every conditional.
bukhari:2205.ur: The Urdu cases are embedded in the attributed prohibition and expressly resumed by آپ ... ان تمام قسموں. Retaining them avoids dropping the actual objects of that concluding prohibition. No general legal commentary follows.

bukhari:2207.hi: Anas transmits the five named transaction prohibitions. They are the actual supplied list, not glossary apparatus; retain all five and the literal names.
bukhari:2207.ur: Anas reports the Prophet five prohibitions, with no supplied term definitions. Preserve the exact Urdu names and chain whole.

bukhari:2209.hi: Ibn Umar reports presence, palm-pith eating, the believing-man tree comparison, his thought, youthful silence and the Prophet answer. The first-person silence-in-deference parenthesis is a finite narrated act and belongs in the report.
bukhari:2209.ur: The complete eyewitness scene includes the actual parenthetic I-remained-silent action and its stated reason. Retain it with the age circumstance, not as dictionary commentary.

bukhari:2210.hi: Anas reports Abu Tayba cupping, the command to give one sa dates as wages, and the masters levy reduction. The wages parenthesis supplies the transaction purpose and remains with this concrete payment report; no legal inference is added.
bukhari:2210.ur: The Urdu account states cupping, dates payment and a request to reduce the levy. The remuneration parenthesis defines why the dates were given and stays as source event scope.

bukhari:2211.hi: Aisha reports Hind question about secretly taking from the stingy Abu Sufyan and the Prophet sufficient-maintenance reply. The good-intention and sufficient-for-you-and-sons limitations are complete actual dialogue.
bukhari:2211.ur: The entire Hindi-like but independently read Urdu field gives Hind question and the expressly attributed answer. Preserve the family, sufficiency and intention limits without adding a legal gloss.

bukhari:2212.hi: Aisha explicitly explains the verse concerning rich/poor orphan guardians. Keep the actual recited transliteration, supplied translation and her attributed explanation. Second-chain and Quran-verse labels are apparatus; parenthetic orphan-consumption and payment-for-service expansions are commentary already clarified by the surrounding guardian report.
bukhari:2212.ur: Aisha own statement contains the actual Arabic verse, Urdu rendering and guardian explanation; none is an external verse locator to delete. Keep those words. Separate only the chain label, Quran-verse label and the two explanatory expansions; preserve damaged closing quotation punctuation.

bukhari:2213.hi: Jabir reports the Prophet preemption rule for undivided property and its boundary/road exception. Both restriction clauses stay whole, with no inferred canonical reference.
bukhari:2213.ur: The complete Urdu report preserves undivided property, established limits and altered paths. All conditions are narration content.

bukhari:2214.hi: Jabir reports the independently numbered preemption rule with its own chain and boundaries/road qualification. Keep separate from2213 and2214.2.
bukhari:2214.ur: This source ID supplies a complete Prophet ruling and its own conditions. Similarity to other IDs does not merge it or supply their omitted bodies.

bukhari:2214.2.ar: The full Arabic consists of بهذا, متابعة and رواه chains with في كل ما لم يقسم / في كل مال fragments. The underlying predicate/report is absent; all of it is wording comparison context.
bukhari:2214.2.en: English explicitly says same as above and prints ellipses around in every joint undivided thing and in every property. It ends without the asserted action or rule. Do not supply the missing above text.
bukhari:2214.2.hi: The entire field contains same-as-that transmissions and in-every-undivided-thing/in-every-property wording fragments only. It never supplies what is being ordered or established. These are prepositional comparison fragments, not a finite independent report; keep source-only.
bukhari:2214.2.ur: All Urdu clauses describe similar transmissions and isolated property-scope wording. The absent rule is not reconstructed from2213/2214. Retain this distinct ID as resolved source-only.
bukhari:2214.2.ur-Latn: The complete Roman field contains the same-as wording and property fragments, then a chain. No substantive predicate is printed. Source-only after actual full reading.

bukhari:2218.hi: Aisha narrates the Sad/Abd paternity dispute, resemblance observation, the Prophet bed-attribution ruling, and Sawda screening instruction and subsequent conduct. Keep the complete coherent dialogue and source damaged words; no moral/legal expansion.
bukhari:2218.ur: The complete Urdu supplies both competing claims, the observed resemblance, judgment and Sawda direction. Preserve all parties and the final never-saw-him statement in their actual narrative roles.

muslim:2162.hi: The opening similar-chain list is a pointer. The Abdul Aziz version then supplies an actual finite rebuke, you did not stop troubling the Messenger. Its speaker and addressee are not named; retain the affirmative variant under that unknown attribution, never as the Prophet own speech.
muslim:2162.ur: The explicit Abdul Aziz variant contains a finite rebuke about burdening the Messenger. Keep the variant introducer and utterance; the earlier same-chain pointer is context. No speaker is borrowed from an adjacent record.

muslim:2163.hi: Umm Atiyya reports the pledge against wailing and which women upheld it. Preserve the printed five/list/alternative wording without reconciling the number or names. Bin Sirin is an identity gloss. The kama-haqqahu fully qualifier limits the compliance claim and stays.
muslim:2163.ur: The own Urdu complete pledge report has damaged spacing/names and a literal alternative between listed women. Keep it unchanged. Bin Sirin is context; kama-haqqahu is the material degree qualifier for adherence, not dispensable apparatus.

muslim:2164.hi: Umm Atiyya reports the pledge and five exceptions, naming Umm Sulaym. The fully qualifier remains. The repeated parenthetic five only restates the already supplied count and is a clarifying gloss.
muslim:2164.ur: The source prints حضرت عطیہ rather than adding Umm in this field; preserve that own name. Keep the complete pledge/degree/five exception statement. The repeated parenthetic five is explanatory context, not a new count.

muslim:2166.hi: Umm Atiyya gives the finite passive funeral-following prohibition with the express not-strict qualification. The prohibiting agent is unnamed in this field; no direct Prophetic attribution is inserted.
muslim:2166.ur: The full Urdu reports being stopped from following funerals but not strictly ordered. The qualification is part of the actual testimony and the unnamed authority stays unnamed.

muslim:2167.hi: Hafsa transmits Umm Atiyya passive prohibition/non-strictness report. It is finite supplied practice, with no named commanding agent to infer.
muslim:2167.ur: Preserve the exact source spelling حجرت and the complete non-strictness qualification. This own field names no ultimate prohibiting speaker.

muslim:2168.hi: Umm Atiyya gives the complete visit during washing, three/five/more conditional instruction, water/beri material, camphor, notification and garment instruction. The leaf parenthesis specifies the supplied washing material and stays with the practical instruction.
muslim:2168.ur: The complete Urdu source supplies all washing conditions and the garment reply despite broken punctuation. The leaf material qualifier is retained; no daughter name or omitted closing quotes are manufactured.

muslim:2169.hi: Umm Atiyya gives a finite we-combed-and-made-three-plaits observation. The person whose hair was arranged is not identified in this own short field. Preserve the literal लातें typo and do not name a daughter.
muslim:2169.ur: The actual reported combing and three plaits remain. The hair parenthesis repeats the object already implied by combing/plaits and is lexical clarification; the unnamed person remains unfilled.

muslim:2170.hi: The initial death of one Prophet daughter and two actual affirmative opening variants are supplied. Ibn Ulayya has arrival during washing; Malik has arrival after death. Keep them as transmitted variants of one family, not separate eyewitness acts by the transmitters. The repeated Umm Atiyya identifier and final same-as chain tail are context.
muslim:2170.ur: Three supplied report fragments remain in order. The yuun and repeated Umm Atiyya parentheses are introduction/identity glosses; the final same-as chain is a bare pointer. Preserve each actual difference without completing the omitted remainder.

muslim:2171.hi: After a same-report pointer, an unnamed respectful-pronoun speaker directs three/five/seven/more washes. The parenthetic wash verb is the actual supplied predicate and must remain. The field then literally prints Hafsa saying to Umm Atiyya we made three plaits; do not repair that speaker relationship from a familiar parallel.
muslim:2171.ur: The directive is supplied but its actor is only آپ. Keep the parenthetic غسل دینا because it supplies the operation being counted. The following Hafsa-to-Umm-Atiyya attribution remains as printed. The parenthetic hair object is explanatory; the complete plait act remains.

muslim:2172.hi: Ibn Ulayya/Ayyub/Hafsa transmission explicitly supplies the Messenger name inside parentheses, so it remains as the only named authority for the washing directive. The reporting-while clause clarifies the actual transmission relation and stays. Ismail is an identity gloss. Umm Atiyya own three-plait observation is a second component.
muslim:2172.ur: The parenthetic Messenger and بیان کرتے ہوئے are material attribution/frame qualifiers, not erased by a blanket parenthesis rule. Ismail and the hair-object gloss are context. Keep the actual odd-number directive and separately attributed Umm Atiyya braiding.

muslim:2174.hi: First a full arrival/washing and odd-five-or-more Prophet instruction is supplied; then a similar-meaning pointer; then an actual three-part braiding addition. Retain the two finite fragments separately in one family. Repeated speaker identification is context. Hindi lacks the Urdu detailed side/front continuation and is not completed.
muslim:2174.ur: Keep the actual washing directive and the later finite braiding addition, including the own Urdu two sides/front detail. Omit the Ayyub/Asim same-meaning bridge and redundant parenthetic Umm Atiyya identification. No omitted earlier body is imported.

muslim:2179.hi: Aisha supplies the three-cloth shrouding and hulla confusion/account. Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr then takes the hulla, states his own intended use, revises that intention and sells it for charity. Keep separate attribution components. Urwa/Yemen/hulla-definition/that-hulla/storage clarification and expanded arranging wording are explanatory parentheses; all actual counterfactual and charity predicates remain.
muslim:2179.ur: The Urdu full narrative independently supplies Aisha account and Abdullah quoted intention/reconsideration. Preserve sale and monetary charity, not the next record garment-donation wording. Separate only the six exact identity/geographic/lexical expansions, retaining the conditional statement itself.

muslim:2180.hi: Urwa, through Hisham own father link, supplies the temporary wrapping and replacement by three white cloths; no Aisha link is printed here. Abdullah then speaks and gives the garment away. Keep both components and the rhetorical statement exact; Urwa and kafn definition parentheses are context.
muslim:2180.ur: The whole own Urdu has Urwa transmission without Aisha, and the hulla itself donated rather than sold. Preserve these differences. The two explanatory parentheses do not carry independent action; actual wrapping, unwrapping, shrouding and charity remain.

muslim:2181.ar: The complete Arabic chains conclude بأن the Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr story is not in their hadith. No supplied action/matn body follows; preserve as source-only transmission apparatus.
muslim:2181.en: English says the same chain and no mention of Abdullah story, without giving the actual narrative. Full field read, source-only.
muslim:2181.hi: The entire field lists same-chain transmitters and says their version lacks Abdullah story. It supplies no affirmative underlying report; resolved source-only after reading all siblings.
muslim:2181.ur: The complete Urdu is a similar-chain/omitted-story note. The negated presence of a story is editorial transmission comparison, not the missing narrative itself.
muslim:2181.ur-Latn: The full Roman field lists transmitters and explicitly omits Abdullah story. No body is supplied; preserve source-only.

muslim:2183.hi: Aisha reports that the deceased Messenger was covered with a striped Yemeni sheet. Bin Kaysan and Zuhri are identity glosses, not parts of the event; preserve all remaining wording.
muslim:2183.ur: The full Urdu has a malformed parenthesis beginning before Zuhri and closing only after the entire report. Do not discard the report as parenthetical. Remove only the identity label/opening fragment and its stranded final closing glyph, plus the separate Bin Kaysan label; keep the source chain and complete Aisha statement.

muslim:2215.hi: Abu Hurayra report supplies the woman/youth uncertainty, Prophet inquiry and grave prayer, but Hindi omits a clear initial or and the opening/attribution of the final light-in-graves speech. Retain the coherent story through the funeral prayer; keep the orphaned final because/light tail as reviewed context rather than fill it from Urdu. Sahaba is an identity gloss.
muslim:2215.ur: Urdu supplies the complete woman-or-young-man uncertainty, inquiry, prayer and a fully introduced Prophetic speech about dark graves and illumination through his prayer. Retain that full speech as a distinct component in the same event. Sahaba and graves-repeat parentheses are explanatory identifiers.

muslim:2222.hi: Jabir reports standing for a Jewish woman funeral, the question and the Prophet death/fear and stand instruction. The parenthetic funeral repeats the already stated event and is context. The cause-of qualifier in the fear statement retains its causal predication and stays.
muslim:2222.ur: The Urdu complete dialogue has the Jewish woman funeral and stand-at-funerals instruction. Retain the cause-of fear qualifier within the actual reply; remove only the redundant funeral label. No absent rationale is introduced.

muslim:2229.ar: All Arabic words are the Abu Kurayb/Ibn Abi Zaida/Yahya chain and بهذا الإسناد; there is no matn predicate.
muslim:2229.en: The full English is only narrated-by-Yahya with the same chain. It supplies no substantive report.
muslim:2229.hi: The complete Hindi consists only of Ibn Abi Zaidah from Yahya, same-chain same-report. No report body is printed.
muslim:2229.ur: The complete Urdu is solely the same-chain pointer. Do not infer a funeral action or earlier report from a neighboring number.
muslim:2229.ur-Latn: The complete Roman Urdu is the same-chain/same-report pointer only. Preserve it source-only.
